hero.heading: Broadford Cemetery
hero.body: The Broadford Cemetery is situated in Piper Street Broadford, Victoria and is administered by the Broadford Cemetery Trust (Volunteers) under the Department of Health, Victoria.

quote: Broadford Cemetery is not just a resting place for the dead; it is a place of comfort, contemplation and conversation for our community.

care.heading: A cemetery in continuous care since 1867
care.body:
In July 1867 the Government Gazette announced the first three trustees for the land which had been put aside in March of that year. The cemetery has been managed by a Trust without interruption ever since — first by representatives of the local churches, and today by volunteers drawn from across the Broadford community.

The grounds have grown steadily: a lawn section in the 1970s, the niche wall for ashes, memorial rose gardens, the Dorothy Drysdale memorial garden in 2006, and a second lawn section, babies section and further rose garden between 2019 and 2020.

figure.alt: A row of pink prunus trees in full blossom along the cemetery’s white boundary fence, with white-painted iron grave surrounds behind, under a blue spring sky.
figure.caption: Prunus in blossom along the boundary fence.

speak.heading: Need to speak to someone?
speak.body: The Trust is run entirely by volunteers. Email is the fastest way to reach us, and we will reply as soon as a trustee is able.

notice.label: Arranging a burial
notice.body: If you are arranging a funeral, your funeral director will usually deal with the Trust for you. If you would rather speak to us directly, or you are enquiring about a plot, please write to us and a trustee will come back to you.

support.heading: Support the cemetery
support.body:
Your donation will be used to build new infrastructure with paving in the centre of our cemetery. Engraved pavers are available in single, double and triple sizes and are laid permanently in the shelter area.

A paver stays where it is laid. It becomes part of the cemetery’s own fabric — walked past, read and remembered by everyone who comes through the shelter, for as long as the cemetery stands. Many families choose one to mark a name that is already here, or simply to leave something lasting for the place.

figure.alt: The cemetery’s open shelter with a green roof and timber bench, standing on a brick-paved slab in front of the brick niche wall, with young standard roses in the lawn.
figure.caption: The shelter and niche wall. Engraved pavers are laid in the brick paving of the shelter area.
